topics.title: How a Chip Factory Prints Billions of Switches With Light

demand.title: Semiconductor Chip कैसे बनती है? रेत से 2nm Chip तक की पूरी कहानी

topics.hook: To print a modern chip, a machine blasts drops of molten tin fifty thousand times a second.
topics.angle: Inside ASML's EUV machine: tin droplets hit twice by a laser, plasma giving off 13.5 nm light, mirrors carrying it onto a mask and down onto the wafer, layer by layer. ASML's figures; no export-control politics.

topics.title: How an SSD Stores a Bit With No Moving Parts

demand.title: How do microSD Cards Store 2 TB in such a TINY space?

topics.hook: Your files are electrons trapped in a cage far too small to see. Here's how one gets in and out.
topics.angle: One NAND cell: trapped charge sets a 0 or 1, the read checks it, then 3D stacking piles hundreds of layers (332 in KIOXIA's 2025 generation, from 48 in 2015) into a skyscraper. Keep layers and stacked dies apart (viewers caught that slip before).

topics.title: How Your Message Crosses the Ocean in a Tenth of a Second

demand.title: Inside America's Only Internet Sea Cable Maker

topics.hook: Your message to London didn't go to space. It went along the bottom of the Atlantic, in a cable as wide as a garden hose.
topics.angle: From your phone to a landing station, into a fibre pair, light pulses along MAREA's 6,605 km of Atlantic floor, boosted by repeaters, out at Bilbao. Light moves at the speed of light in glass, not in a vacuum (viewers correct this). Any travel time is computed from the length and a sourced speed.
